answer: Sybil resistance comes from making coordinated identities costly to operate and dangerous to expose: when k bonded identities equivocate in a correlated way, their slashing penalty grows as O(k²), rather than as a simple per-identity fee. Detection also applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss, amplified by asymmetric depreciation of escrowed collateral. Thus a swarm cannot cheaply diversify risk across names such as meadow, raven, and anchor; shared control creates correlated evidence and concentrates liability.
